question: Which genetic variant sites were classified into multiple different variant types in the Cannabis genomics study of March 2017?
SQL: SELECT variant_id FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 GROUP BY variant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TYPE) > 1;

question: In the March 2017 study of cannabis genomics, for each genetic variant type, which variant site has the highest allele frequency?
SQL: SELECT TYPE, variant_id FROM ( SELECT TYPE, variant_id, AF, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TYPE ORDER BY AF DESC) AS rn FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In the cannabis genomics project, which samples from March 2017 have raw project information that is not recorded in the detailed sample information table, possibly due to incomplete annotation or data incompleteness?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT Sample_Name FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.CS3K_PROJECT_INFO p WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.SAMPLE_INFO_201703 s WHERE s.SRA_Sample_s = p.Sample_Name );

question: Which samples' raw data from March 2017 in the cannabis genomics project were simultaneously recorded in the detailed sample information table?
SQL: SELECT SRA_Sample FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.CS3K_PROJECT_INFO WHERE SRA_Sample IN (SELECT SRA_Sample_s FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.SAMPLE_INFO_201703);

question: In the March 2017 study on cannabis genomics, for each type of genetic variation, which variant sites have allele frequencies significantly higher than the general level of that type, potentially being hotspots of natural selection?
SQL: SELECT variant_id FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 t1 WHERE AF > (SELECT AVG(AF) FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 t2 WHERE t2.TYPE = t1.TYPE);

question: In the March 2017 cannabis genomics study, which variant sites have the highest sequencing depth under each type of genetic variation and are considered high-confidence detection sites?
SQL: WITH ranked AS ( SELECT TYPE AS Category, variant_id AS Entity, DP AS Measure, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY TYPE ORDER BY DP DESC) AS quintile FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 WHERE DP IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity FROM ranked WHERE quintile = 1;

question: In the March 2017 study on cannabis genomics, for each type of genetic variation, which variant sites have allele frequencies not only higher than the average level of that type but also predominantly reflect the main characteristics of that variation type? Please list the top five sites with the most prominent contribution in each variation category.
SQL: WITH category_stats AS ( SELECT TYPE AS Category, AVG(AF) AS avg_measure, SUM(AF) AS total_measure FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 GROUP BY TYPE ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.TYPE AS Category, t.variant_id AS Entity, t.AF AS Measure, cs.avg_measure, cs.total_measure, t.AF / cs.total_measure * 100 AS pct_of_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.TYPE ORDER BY t.AF / cs.total_measure DESC) AS rn FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 t JOIN category_stats cs ON t.TYPE = cs.Category WHERE t.AF > cs.avg_measure ) SELECT Category, Entity, pct_of_total FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the cannabis genomics study from March 2017, for each variant type, where are the three loci with the highest allele frequencies located? How much higher are their frequencies compared to the average frequency of the same variant type, and could they be important functional loci?
SQL: WITH type_avg AS ( SELECT TYPE AS Category, AVG(AF) AS avg_af FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 GROUP BY TYPE ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.TYPE AS Category, t.variant_id AS Entity, t.AF AS Measure, ta.avg_af, (t.AF - ta.avg_af) / ta.avg_af * 100 AS pct_above_avg, t.start, t.DP, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.TYPE ORDER BY t.AF DESC) AS rn FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 t JOIN type_avg ta ON t.TYPE = ta.Category WHERE t.AF IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity, Measure, avg_af, pct_above_avg, start, DP FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

question: In the cannabis genomics study of March 2017, for each type of genetic variant, which variant loci exhibit a significant leap in sequencing depth along chromosomal positions, becoming hotspot regions where detection confidence dramatically increases? Please list the top five loci with the largest jump magnitude within each variant type.
SQL: WITH lagged AS ( SELECT TYPE, variant_id, start, DP, LAG(DP) OVER ( PARTITION BY TYPE ORDER BY start ASC ) AS prev_depth FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 WHERE DP IS NOT NULL AND start IS NOT NULL ), growth AS ( SELECT TYPE, variant_id, start, DP, prev_depth, ROUND((DP - prev_depth) / NULLIF(prev_depth, 0) * 100, 2) AS jump_rate FROM lagged WHERE prev_depth IS NOT NULL AND prev_depth > 0 AND DP > prev_depth ), ranked AS ( SELECT TYPE AS Category, variant_id AS Entity, jump_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TYPE ORDER BY jump_rate DESC) AS rn FROM growth ) SELECT Category, Entity, jump_rate FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the Cannabis genomics study of March 2017, what are the three variant types with the highest total sequencing depth?
SQL: SELECT TYPE AS Category, SUM(DP) AS total_depth FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 GROUP BY TYPE ORDER BY total_depth DESC LIMIT 3;

question: What are the top three organisms with the most samples in the cannabis genomics project?
SQL: SELECT Organism AS Category, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.CS3K_PROJECT_INFO GROUP BY Organism ORDER BY record_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: In the March 2017 study of cannabis genomics, for each variant type, which loci have allele frequencies that are high-frequency within that type that significantly higher than most other loci?
SQL: WITH type_q3 AS ( SELECT TYPE AS Category, MIN(AF) AS q3 FROM ( SELECT TYPE, AF, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY TYPE ORDER BY AF) AS pr FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 ) t WHERE pr >= 0.75 GROUP BY TYPE ) SELECT t.TYPE, t.variant_id, t.AF, t.start, t.DP FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 t JOIN type_q3 q ON t.TYPE = q.Category WHERE t.AF > q.q3;

question: In the 1000 Genomes project, which five samples have the highest Indel Ratio?
SQL: SELECT Sample FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO ORDER BY LC_Indel_Ratio DESC LIMIT 5;

question: In _1000_GENOMES, which sample has the highest insertion-deletion ratio in each super population?
SQL: SELECT Super_Population, Sample FROM ( SELECT Super_Population, Sample, LC_Indel_Ratio, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Super_Population ORDER BY LC_Indel_Ratio DESC) AS rn FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In _1000_GENOMES, which samples have an abnormally high frequency of indel mutations?
SQL: SELECT Sample FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO WHERE LC_Indel_Ratio > (SELECT AVG(LC_Indel_Ratio) FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO);

question: In the _1000_GENOMES dataset, which samples lack corresponding family pedigree records and thus may not be usable for family-based genetic analysis?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT Sample FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO s WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM _1000_GENOMES.PEDIGREE p WHERE p.Individual_ID = s.Sample );

question: In _1000_GENOMES, which samples in the family pedigree records are available for genetic linkage analysis?
SQL: SELECT Sample FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO WHERE Sample IN (SELECT Individual_ID FROM _1000_GENOMES.PEDIGREE);

question: Within each superpopulation in _1000_GENOMES, which samples have significantly higher indel ratios than the population average, potentially indicating genomic instability?
SQL: SELECT Sample FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t1 WHERE LC_Indel_Ratio > (SELECT AVG(LC_Indel_Ratio) FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t2 WHERE t2.Super_Population = t1.Super_Population);

question: In _1000_GENOMES, which samples in each super-population have the largest sequencing data volume and serve as benchmark samples for deep sequencing?
SQL: WITH ranked AS ( SELECT Super_Population AS Category, Sample AS Entity, Total_LC_Sequence AS Measure, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY Super_Population ORDER BY Total_LC_Sequence DESC) AS quintile FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO WHERE Total_LC_Sequence IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity FROM ranked WHERE quintile = 1;

question: Within the _1000_GENOMES project, for each superpopulation, which samples have sequencing data volumes that are not only above the average level of that population but also serve as major contributors to the total sequencing data of that population? Please list the top five samples with the largest contribution within each superpopulation.
SQL: WITH category_stats AS ( SELECT Super_Population AS Category, AVG(Total_LC_Sequence) AS avg_measure, SUM(Total_LC_Sequence) AS total_measure FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO GROUP BY Super_Population ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.Super_Population AS Category, t.Sample AS Entity, t.Total_LC_Sequence AS Measure, cs.avg_measure, cs.total_measure, t.Total_LC_Sequence / cs.total_measure * 100 AS pct_of_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.Super_Population ORDER BY t.Total_LC_Sequence / cs.total_measure DESC) AS rn FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t JOIN category_stats cs ON t.Super_Population = cs.Category WHERE t.Total_LC_Sequence > cs.avg_measure ) SELECT Category, Entity, pct_of_total FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the 1000 Genomes Project, which samples have sequencing data volumes far exceeding the typical level of their population, are also present in the family information, and may become core samples for genetic linkage analysis?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT Super_Population, Total_LC_Sequence FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO ORDER BY Super_Population, Total_LC_Sequence ), category_arrays AS ( SELECT Super_Population, JSON_ARRAYAGG(Total_LC_Sequence) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY Super_Population ), category_median AS ( SELECT Super_Population, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) ) AS median_seq FROM category_arrays ) SELECT t.Super_Population, t.Sample, t.Total_LC_Sequence, t.Population, t.LC_Passed_QC FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t JOIN category_median m ON t.Super_Population = m.Super_Population WHERE t.Total_LC_Sequence > m.median_seq AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM _1000_GENOMES.PEDIGREE p WHERE p.Individual_ID = t.Sample );

question: In the _1000_GENOMES dataset, for each superpopulation, which specific population do the samples with the highest sequencing data volume belong to? How much higher is their sequencing depth than the average of that population, and are they considered high-quality reference samples?
SQL: WITH super_avg AS ( SELECT Super_Population AS Category, AVG(Total_LC_Sequence) AS avg_seq FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO GROUP BY Super_Population ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.Super_Population AS Category, t.Sample AS Entity, t.Total_LC_Sequence AS Measure, sa.avg_seq, (t.Total_LC_Sequence - sa.avg_seq) / sa.avg_seq * 100 AS pct_above_avg, t.Population, t.LC_Passed_QC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.Super_Population ORDER BY t.Total_LC_Sequence DESC) AS rn FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t JOIN super_avg sa ON t.Super_Population = sa.Category WHERE t.Total_LC_Sequence IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity, Measure, avg_seq, pct_above_avg, Population, LC_Passed_QC FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

question: Which three super populations in `_1000_GENOMES` have the largest total sequencing data?
SQL: SELECT Super_Population AS Category, SUM(Total_LC_Sequence) AS total_seq FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO GROUP BY Super_Population ORDER BY total_seq DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Which are the top three specific populations with the largest sample sizes in _1000_GENOMES?
SQL: SELECT Population AS Category, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO GROUP BY Population ORDER BY record_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: In _1000_GENOMES, for each super population, which samples rank in the top 25% by sequencing data volume and serve as benchmark samples for deep sequencing?
SQL: WITH super_q3 AS ( SELECT Super_Population AS Category, MIN(Total_LC_Sequence) AS q3 FROM ( SELECT Super_Population, Total_LC_Sequence, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Super_Population ORDER BY Total_LC_Sequence) AS pr FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO ) t WHERE pr >= 0.75 GROUP BY Super_Population ) SELECT t.Super_Population, t.Sample, t.Total_LC_Sequence, t.Population FROM _1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO t JOIN super_q3 q ON t.Super_Population = q.Category WHERE t.Total_LC_Sequence > q.q3;

question: In the gene learning within Open_Targets_Genetics_1, which study sources report the highest number of cases? List the top five.

SQL: SELECT source FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY source HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT trait_category) > 1;

question: In the genetic study in Open_Targets_Genetics_1, for each disease trait, which research institution reported the largest number of cases?
SQL: SELECT trait_category, source FROM ( SELECT trait_category, source, n_cases, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY trait_category ORDER BY n_cases DESC) AS rn FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: Among the gene studies in Open_Targets_Genetics_1, which research institutions have achieved case scales comparable to large-scale clinical trials (exceeding the average level)?
SQL: SELECT source FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES WHERE n_cases > (SELECT AVG(n_cases) FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES);

question: Which sources of research findings from the gene study in OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1 were not incorporated into the subsequent GWAS analysis dataset, possibly because they were not selected or the data failed quality control?

question: Which sources of results from the gene learning in OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1 were incorporated into the subsequent GWAS analysis dataset?

question: In gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease/trait category, which source studies have case sizes exceeding the average size of similar studies and thus possess greater statistical power?
SQL: SELECT source FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t1 WHERE n_cases > (SELECT AVG(n_cases) FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t2 WHERE t2.trait_category = t1.trait_category);

question: In the gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, which source institution completed the most recently published research for each disease trait?
SQL: SELECT trait_category, source FROM ( SELECT trait_category, source, pub_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY trait_category ORDER BY pub_date DESC) AS rn FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In gene studies within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease trait, which research institutions have a moderate case size—neither small-scale exploratory nor large-scale validation (falling between the 30th and 70th percentiles)—representing the typical study scale in the field?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT trait_category, n_cases FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES ORDER BY trait_category, n_cases ), cat_arrays AS ( SELECT trait_category, JSON_ARRAYAGG(n_cases) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY trait_category ), cat_percentiles AS ( SELECT trait_category, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.3, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) ) AS p30, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.7, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) ) AS p70 FROM cat_arrays ) SELECT t.trait_category, t.source, t.n_cases, t.study_id, t.pub_date FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN cat_percentiles cp ON t.trait_category = cp.trait_category WHERE t.n_cases BETWEEN cp.p30 AND cp.p70;

question: In OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1 for gene learning, within each disease trait category, which research institutions have published new studies in consecutive years, demonstrating sustained research investment?
SQL: WITH yearly_records AS ( SELECT DISTINCT trait_category AS Category, source AS Entity, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pub_date) AS Time FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES WHERE pub_date IS NOT NULL ), with_prev AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, LAG(Time) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Time) AS prev_time FROM yearly_records ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM with_prev WHERE prev_time IS NOT NULL AND Time - prev_time = 1;

question: In the gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, which research institutions have published three consecutive studies with progressively larger case sizes, reflecting sustained research investment?
SQL: WITH base AS ( SELECT source AS Entity, pub_date AS Time, n_cases AS Measure, LAG(n_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY pub_date) AS prev1, LAG(n_cases, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY pub_date) AS prev2 FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES WHERE pub_date IS NOT NULL AND n_cases IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DISTINCT Entity FROM base WHERE prev2 IS NOT NULL AND Measure > prev1 AND prev1 > prev2;

question: In gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each type of disease trait, which research institutions have case sizes that rank in the top tier (top 20%) and serve as core data contributors in this field?
SQL: WITH ranked AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, source AS Entity, n_cases AS Measure, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY trait_category ORDER BY n_cases DESC) AS quintile FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES WHERE n_cases IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity FROM ranked WHERE quintile = 1;

question: In OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1 for gene learning, within each disease trait category, which research institutions not only have case sample sizes above the average of similar studies but also account for a significant proportion of total case numbers in that disease area? List the top five institutions contributing most prominently in each disease category.
SQL: WITH category_stats AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, AVG(n_cases) AS avg_measure, SUM(n_cases) AS total_measure FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY trait_category ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.trait_category AS Category, t.source AS Entity, t.n_cases AS Measure, cs.avg_measure, cs.total_measure, t.n_cases / cs.total_measure * 100 AS pct_of_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.trait_category ORDER BY t.n_cases / cs.total_measure DESC) AS rn FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN category_stats cs ON t.trait_category = cs.Category WHERE t.n_cases > cs.avg_measure ) SELECT Category, Entity, pct_of_total FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the gene study within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, which research institutions have case numbers far exceeding the typical scale of similar studies (greater than 50%), and these data are also incorporated into subsequent GWAS analyses, potentially contributing more to genetic discoveries?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT trait_category, n_cases FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES ORDER BY trait_category, n_cases ), category_arrays AS ( SELECT trait_category, JSON_ARRAYAGG(n_cases) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY trait_category ), category_median AS ( SELECT trait_category, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) ) AS median_cases FROM category_arrays ) SELECT t.trait_category, t.source, t.n_cases, t.study_id, t.pub_date FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN category_median m ON t.trait_category = m.trait_category WHERE t.n_cases > m.median_cases AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_SA_GWAS s WHERE s.study_id = t.study_id );

question: In the gene study in OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease trait category, which are the top three research institutions with the largest number of cases? How much higher are their case numbers compared to the average case scale of similar studies, and do they have a significant data advantage? Display the trait category, source, case size, average case size, percentage by which the case size exceeds the average, study ID, publication date, and other information.
SQL: WITH category_avg AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, AVG(n_cases) AS avg_cases FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY trait_category ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.trait_category AS Category, t.source AS Entity, t.n_cases AS Measure, ca.avg_cases, (t.n_cases - ca.avg_cases) / ca.avg_cases * 100 AS pct_above_avg, t.study_id, t.pub_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.trait_category ORDER BY t.n_cases DESC) AS rn FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN category_avg ca ON t.trait_category = ca.Category WHERE t.n_cases IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity, Measure, avg_cases, pct_above_avg, study_id, pub_date FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

question: In the gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease trait category, which research institutions have rapidly expanded their case sizes in a short period, demonstrating strong research expansion trend? For each disease category, list the top five institutions with the most rapid growth, showing the trait category, source, and growth rate.
SQL: WITH lagged AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, source AS Entity, pub_date AS Time, n_cases AS Measure, LAG(n_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY trait_category, source ORDER BY pub_date) AS prev_measure FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES WHERE n_cases IS NOT NULL AND pub_date IS NOT NULL ), growth AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, (Measure - prev_measure) / NULLIF(prev_measure, 0) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM lagged WHERE prev_measure IS NOT NULL AND prev_measure > 0 ), ranked AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY growth_rate DESC) AS rn FROM growth ) SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the gene learning of OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, which three disease trait categories have the highest total number of cases, and what are their corresponding counts?
SQL: SELECT trait_category AS Category, SUM(n_cases) AS total_cases FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY trait_category ORDER BY total_cases DESC LIMIT 3;

question: In the gene learning in OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, which are the top three ancestral groups with the most studies, and what are the corresponding counts?
SQL: SELECT ancestry_initial AS Category, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY ancestry_initial ORDER BY record_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: In gene learning within OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease trait category, which research institutions have case sample sizes that belong to the leading group in the field, significantly larger than most similar studies (greater than 75%)? The results should display disease trait category, source, case sample size, study ID, and release date.
SQL: WITH cat_q3 AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, MIN(n_cases) AS q3 FROM ( SELECT trait_category, n_cases, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY trait_category ORDER BY n_cases) AS pr FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES ) t WHERE pr >= 0.75 GROUP BY trait_category ) SELECT t.trait_category, t.source, t.n_cases, t.study_id, t.pub_date FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN cat_q3 q ON t.trait_category = q.Category WHERE t.n_cases > q.q3;

question: In the gene learning in OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1, for each disease trait category, which research institutions' case scales have exceeded the field’s average level for that year for two consecutive years, demonstrating sustained research capability? The results need to include the medical record trait category and source.
SQL: WITH yearly_avg AS ( SELECT trait_category AS Category, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pub_date) AS Year, AVG(n_cases) AS avg_cases FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES GROUP BY trait_category, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pub_date) ), above_avg AS ( SELECT t.trait_category AS Category, t.source AS Entity, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.pub_date) AS Year, t.n_cases AS Measure, CASE WHEN t.n_cases > ya.avg_cases THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS above FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_1.GENETICS_STUDIES t JOIN yearly_avg ya ON t.trait_category = ya.Category AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.pub_date) = ya.Year ), consecutive AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Year, above, LAG(above) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Year) AS prev_above FROM above_avg ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM consecutive WHERE above = 1 AND prev_above = 1;

question: According to the U.S. birth naming data from 1910 to 2013, which five states had the highest total number of births?

question: In the U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which states have records for both male and female births?

question: In the birth population statistics of the United States from 1910 to 2013, which state had the highest number of male births, and which state had the highest number of female births?

question: According to U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which states have historically been truly populous states?

question: According to the United States birth records from 1910 to 2013, in which states were the latest statistics recorded for male and female infants, respectively?
SQL: SELECT gender, state FROM ( SELECT gender, state, year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY year DESC) AS rn FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: Based on U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, among male and female infant groups, which states had annual birth counts that fell into the typical range for that gender, reflecting a common population size rather than extreme large or small states?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT gender, number FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 ORDER BY gender, number ), gender_arrays AS ( SELECT gender, JSON_ARRAYAGG(number) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY gender ), gender_percentiles AS ( SELECT gender, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.3, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) ) AS p30, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.7, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) ) AS p70 FROM gender_arrays ) SELECT t.gender, t.state, t.number, t.year FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN gender_percentiles gp ON t.gender = gp.gender WHERE t.number BETWEEN gp.p30 AND gp.p70;

question: Based on U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, for male and female infant groups, which states have birth counts in every consecutive year, forming a complete population change trajectory?
SQL: WITH yearly_records AS ( SELECT DISTINCT gender AS Category, state AS Entity, year AS Time FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 WHERE year IS NOT NULL ), with_prev AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, LAG(Time) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Time) AS prev_time FROM yearly_records ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM with_prev WHERE prev_time IS NOT NULL AND Time - prev_time = 1;

question: Based on the birth records of the United States from 1910 to 2013, which states experienced three consecutive years of rising annual birth numbers, possibly corresponding to population influx waves?
SQL: WITH base AS ( SELECT state AS Entity, year AS Time, number AS Measure, LAG(number, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY year) AS prev1, LAG(number, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY year) AS prev2 FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 WHERE year IS NOT NULL AND number IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DISTINCT Entity FROM base WHERE prev2 IS NOT NULL AND Measure > prev1 AND prev1 > prev2;

question: Based on U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which states had the highest numbers of male and female births, respectively, making them the top representatives among populous states?
SQL: WITH ranked AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, state AS Entity, number AS Measure, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY number DESC) AS quintile FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 WHERE number IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity FROM ranked WHERE quintile = 1;

question: Based on U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which states among male and female infant groups not only have birth counts exceeding the gender-specific average but also account for a significant share of that gender's total births? Please list the top five states with the largest contributions separately for male and female groups.
SQL: WITH category_stats AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, AVG(number) AS avg_measure, SUM(number) AS total_measure FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 GROUP BY gender ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.gender AS Category, t.state AS Entity, t.number AS Measure, cs.avg_measure, cs.total_measure, t.number / cs.total_measure * 100 AS pct_of_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.gender ORDER BY t.number / cs.total_measure DESC) AS rn FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN category_stats cs ON t.gender = cs.Category WHERE t.number > cs.avg_measure ) SELECT Category, Entity, pct_of_total FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: According to U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which states had annual birth counts that stood out prominently within the male or female infant groups, far exceeding typical levels for that gender, possibly indicating concentrations of population influx or baby booms?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT gender, number FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 ORDER BY gender, number ), gender_arrays AS ( SELECT gender, JSON_ARRAYAGG(number) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY gender ), category_median AS ( SELECT gender, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) ) AS median_number FROM gender_arrays ) SELECT t.gender, t.state, t.number, t.year FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN category_median m ON t.gender = m.gender WHERE t.number > m.median_number;

question: Based on U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, for male and female infants respectively, in which years and states were the birth numbers particularly prominent? By how many percentage points did the birth scale in these states exceed the national average for that gender?
SQL: WITH gender_avg AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, AVG(number) AS avg_number FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 GROUP BY gender ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.gender AS Category, t.state AS Entity, t.number AS Measure, ga.avg_number, (t.number - ga.avg_number) / ga.avg_number * 100 AS pct_above_avg, t.year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.gender ORDER BY t.number DESC) AS rn FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN gender_avg ga ON t.gender = ga.Category WHERE t.number IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity, Measure, avg_number, pct_above_avg, year FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

question: Based on the birth records in the United States from 1910 to 2013, among male and female infant populations, which states experienced explosive annual birth increases that may correspond to immigration waves or baby booms? Please list the top five states with the most significant increases for the male and female groups, respectively.
SQL: WITH lagged AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, state AS Entity, year AS Time, number AS Measure, LAG(number) OVER (PARTITION BY gender, state ORDER BY year) AS prev_measure FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 WHERE number IS NOT NULL AND year IS NOT NULL ), growth AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, (Measure - prev_measure) / NULLIF(prev_measure, 0) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM lagged WHERE prev_measure IS NOT NULL AND prev_measure > 0 ), ranked AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY growth_rate DESC) AS rn FROM growth ) SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: According to U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, which three states had the highest total number of births?
SQL: SELECT state AS Category, SUM(number) AS total_births FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 GROUP BY state ORDER BY total_births DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Based on the U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, what are the top three states with the most entries?
SQL: SELECT state AS Category, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 GROUP BY state ORDER BY record_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Based on the U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, among the male and female infant cohorts, which states had annual birth counts that fell into the highest tier within each gender, far exceeding the levels of normal states?
SQL: WITH gender_q3 AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, MIN(number) AS q3 FROM ( SELECT gender, number, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY number) AS pr FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 ) t WHERE pr >= 0.75 GROUP BY gender ) SELECT t.gender, t.state, t.number, t.year FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN gender_q3 q ON t.gender = q.Category WHERE t.number > q.q3;

question: Based on the U.S. birth records from 1910 to 2013, among male and female infant groups, which states had annual birth numbers that exceeded the national average for that sex in two consecutive years, potentially indicating areas of sustained population growth?
SQL: WITH yearly_avg AS ( SELECT gender AS Category, year AS Year, AVG(number) AS avg_number FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 GROUP BY gender, year ), above_avg AS ( SELECT t.gender AS Category, t.state AS Entity, t.year AS Year, t.number AS Measure, CASE WHEN t.number > ya.avg_number THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS above FROM USA_NAMES.USA_1910_2013 t JOIN yearly_avg ya ON t.gender = ya.Category AND t.year = ya.Year ), consecutive AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Year, above, LAG(above) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Year) AS prev_above FROM above_avg ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM consecutive WHERE above = 1 AND prev_above = 1;

question: In the annual survey of the United States Department of Agriculture, which states rank top five in the production value of livestock products?
SQL: SELECT state_name FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 5;

question: In the USDA survey, which animals have multiple types of statistical data (from the statistical type descriptions)?
SQL: SELECT commodity_desc FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY commodity_desc HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT statisticcat_desc) > 1;

question: In the USDA animal product survey data, what is the record with the maximum value under each industry category?
SQL: SELECT sector_desc, commodity_desc FROM ( SELECT sector_desc, commodity_desc, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sector_desc ORDER BY value DESC) AS rn FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In the annual survey of the United States Department of Agriculture, which states have a livestock product value higher than the average?
SQL: SELECT state_name FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE value > (SELECT AVG(value) FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS);

question: In the USDA survey data, which states' livestock product data were not covered by the 2002 Census of Agriculture, possibly due to census omissions or newly added states?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT state_name FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ap WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.CENSUS_2002 c WHERE c.state_alpha = ap.state_alpha );

question: Which states' livestock product data in the USDA survey are also covered by the 2002 Census of Agriculture?
SQL: SELECT state_name FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE state_alpha IN (SELECT state_alpha FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.CENSUS_2002);

question: Which animal products in each industry category of the USDA survey data have a production value that exceeds the average level of that category, thereby becoming industry benchmarks?
SQL: SELECT commodity_desc FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t1 WHERE value > (SELECT AVG(value) FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t2 WHERE t2.sector_desc = t1.sector_desc);

question: In the USDA animal product survey, which animal was counted in the most recent year?
SQL: SELECT sector_desc, commodity_desc FROM ( SELECT sector_desc, commodity_desc, year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sector_desc ORDER BY year DESC) AS rn FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In the USDA's survey of animal products, within each category, which products have output values at the typical level for that category—neither particularly outstanding nor especially low—representing the backbone of the industry?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT sector_desc, value FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ORDER BY sector_desc, value ), sector_arrays AS ( SELECT sector_desc, JSON_ARRAYAGG(value) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY sector_desc ), sector_percentiles AS ( SELECT sector_desc, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.3, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.3), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.3 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.3))) ) AS p30, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', (cnt-1)*0.7, ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.7), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.7 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.7))) ) AS p70 FROM sector_arrays ) SELECT t.sector_desc, t.commodity_desc, t.value, t.state_name, t.year FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN sector_percentiles sp ON t.sector_desc = sp.sector_desc WHERE t.value BETWEEN sp.p30 AND sp.p70;

question: In the USDA animal product surveys, within each category, which product production values have been recorded in consecutive years, forming a continuous time series?
SQL: WITH yearly_records AS ( SELECT DISTINCT sector_desc AS Category, commodity_desc AS Entity, year AS Time FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE year IS NOT NULL ), with_prev AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, LAG(Time) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Time) AS prev_time FROM yearly_records ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM with_prev WHERE prev_time IS NOT NULL AND Time - prev_time = 1;

question: Which products in the USDA animal products survey had annual output values that increased for three consecutive years, indicating strong market demand?
SQL: WITH base AS ( SELECT commodity_desc AS Entity, year AS Time, value AS Measure, LAG(value, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY commodity_desc ORDER BY year) AS prev1, LAG(value, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY commodity_desc ORDER BY year) AS prev2 FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE year IS NOT NULL AND value IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DISTINCT Entity FROM base WHERE prev2 IS NOT NULL AND Measure > prev1 AND prev1 > prev2;

question: In the USDA's animal and animal products survey, which agricultural products have output values that belong to the first tier and are star products within each industry category?
SQL: WITH ranked AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, commodity_desc AS Entity, value AS Measure, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY sector_desc ORDER BY value DESC) AS quintile FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE value IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity FROM ranked WHERE quintile = 1;

question: In the USDA's Animal and Animal Products survey, within each industry category, which agricultural products have a production value that is not only above the category's average but also accounts for a significant share of the category's total production value? Please list the top five most prominent agricultural products in each category.
SQL: WITH category_stats AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, AVG(value) AS avg_measure, SUM(value) AS total_measure FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY sector_desc ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.sector_desc AS Category, t.commodity_desc AS Entity, t.value AS Measure, cs.avg_measure, cs.total_measure, t.value / cs.total_measure * 100 AS pct_of_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.sector_desc ORDER BY t.value / cs.total_measure DESC) AS rn FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN category_stats cs ON t.sector_desc = cs.Category WHERE t.value > cs.avg_measure ) SELECT Category, Entity, pct_of_total FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the USDA survey of animals and their products, which products have production values significantly higher than the typical level in the same industry, and are from states that also participated in the 2002 Census of Agriculture, making these data potentially more historically comparable?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT sector_desc, value FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ORDER BY sector_desc, value ), sector_arrays AS ( SELECT sector_desc, JSON_ARRAYAGG(value) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY sector_desc ), category_median AS ( SELECT sector_desc, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) ) AS median_value FROM sector_arrays ) SELECT t.sector_desc, t.commodity_desc, t.value, t.state_name, t.year FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN category_median m ON t.sector_desc = m.sector_desc WHERE t.value > m.median_value AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.CENSUS_2002 c WHERE c.state_alpha = t.state_alpha );

question: In the USDA survey of animals and their products, for each industry category, which states and years do the agricultural products with the highest production value come from? By how much do they exceed the average production value of their category, and do they qualify as the far-ahead “冠军作物”?
SQL: WITH sector_avg AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, AVG(value) AS avg_value FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY sector_desc ), ranked AS ( SELECT t.sector_desc AS Category, t.commodity_desc AS Entity, t.value AS Measure, sa.avg_value, (t.value - sa.avg_value) / sa.avg_value * 100 AS pct_above_avg, t.state_name, t.year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.sector_desc ORDER BY t.value DESC) AS rn FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN sector_avg sa ON t.sector_desc = sa.Category WHERE t.value IS NOT NULL ) SELECT Category, Entity, Measure, avg_value, pct_above_avg, state_name, year FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

question: In the USDA's survey of animals and their products, within each industry category, which products' annual production value once experienced a dramatic surge, becoming the brightest stars of that year? Please list the top five products with the strongest growth momentum in each category.
SQL: WITH lagged AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, commodity_desc AS Entity, year AS Time, value AS Measure, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY sector_desc, commodity_desc ORDER BY year) AS prev_measure FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS WHERE value IS NOT NULL AND year IS NOT NULL ), growth AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Time, (Measure - prev_measure) / NULLIF(prev_measure, 0) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM lagged WHERE prev_measure IS NOT NULL AND prev_measure > 0 ), ranked AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY growth_rate DESC) AS rn FROM growth ) SELECT Category, Entity, growth_rate FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 5;

question: In the USDA's survey of animals and their products, which three industry categories have the highest total output value?
SQL: SELECT sector_desc AS Category, SUM(value) AS total_value FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY sector_desc ORDER BY total_value DESC LIMIT 3;

question: What are the top three data aggregation levels with the highest number of record entries in the United States Department of Agriculture's survey of animals and their products?
SQL: SELECT agg_level_desc AS Category, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY agg_level_desc ORDER BY record_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: In the USDA survey of animals and their products, within each industry category, which products' output values rank in the top tier (top 25 percent) of the category, i.e., exceeding the output values of the vast majority of other products?
SQL: WITH sector_q3 AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, MIN(value) AS q3 FROM ( SELECT sector_desc, value, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sector_desc ORDER BY value) AS pr FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS ) t WHERE pr >= 0.75 GROUP BY sector_desc ) SELECT t.sector_desc, t.commodity_desc, t.value, t.state_name, t.year FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN sector_q3 q ON t.sector_desc = q.Category WHERE t.value > q.q3;

question: In the USDA animal and animal product survey data, within each industry category, which products have an output value above the average level of that category for two consecutive years, demonstrating stable market performance?
SQL: WITH yearly_avg AS ( SELECT sector_desc AS Category, year AS Year, AVG(value) AS avg_value FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS GROUP BY sector_desc, year ), above_avg AS ( SELECT t.sector_desc AS Category, t.commodity_desc AS Entity, t.year AS Year, t.value AS Measure, CASE WHEN t.value > ya.avg_value THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS above FROM USDA_NASS_AGRICULTURE.ANIMALS_PRODUCTS t JOIN yearly_avg ya ON t.sector_desc = ya.Category AND t.year = ya.Year ), consecutive AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Year, above, LAG(above) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Year) AS prev_above FROM above_avg ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM consecutive WHERE above = 1 AND prev_above = 1;

question: In the US administrative boundary data, which counties have at least one recorded adjacent-county relationship?
SQL: SELECT county_name FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_US_BOUNDARIES_COUNTIES WHERE county_fips_code IN ( SELECT county_fips_code FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_US_BOUNDARIES_ADJACENT_COUNTIES );

question: For each OpenStreetMap contributor, which map node did they edit most recently?
SQL: SELECT username, id FROM ( SELECT username, id, osm_timestamp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY username ORDER BY osm_timestamp DESC) AS rn FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_PLANET_NODES ) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: In the US ZIP code boundary data, which ZIP code areas have a land area larger than the median land area of all ZIP codes in the same state?
SQL: WITH sorted_values AS ( SELECT state_name, area_land_meters FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_US_BOUNDARIES_ZIP_CODES ORDER BY state_name, area_land_meters ), category_arrays AS ( SELECT state_name, JSON_ARRAYAGG(area_land_meters) AS values_array, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sorted_values GROUP BY state_name ), category_median AS ( SELECT state_name, IF( ABS((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5)) < 1e-9, JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')), JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (1 - ((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) + JSON_EXTRACT(values_array, CONCAT('$[', CEIL((cnt-1)*0.5), ']')) * (((cnt-1)*0.5 - FLOOR((cnt-1)*0.5))) ) AS median_area FROM category_arrays ) SELECT t.state_name, t.zip_code, t.area_land_meters FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_US_BOUNDARIES_ZIP_CODES t JOIN category_median m ON t.state_name = m.state_name WHERE t.area_land_meters > m.median_area;

question: In the OpenStreetMap edit history, for each contributor, which nodes had a version number above that contributor's average for the year in two consecutive years?
SQL: WITH yearly_avg AS ( SELECT username AS Category, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(osm_timestamp AS DATETIME)) AS Year, AVG(version) AS avg_version FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_HISTORY_NODES GROUP BY username, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(osm_timestamp AS DATETIME)) ), above_avg AS ( SELECT t.username AS Category, t.id AS Entity, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t.osm_timestamp AS DATETIME)) AS Year, t.version AS Measure, CASE WHEN t.version > ya.avg_version THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS above FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_HISTORY_NODES t JOIN yearly_avg ya ON t.username = ya.Category AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t.osm_timestamp AS DATETIME)) = ya.Year ), consecutive AS ( SELECT Category, Entity, Year, above, LAG(above) OVER (PARTITION BY Category, Entity ORDER BY Year) AS prev_above FROM above_avg ) SELECT DISTINCT Category, Entity FROM consecutive WHERE above = 1 AND prev_above = 1;
